solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The man's on dope leading to habit

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: a dope is a fool, as is a clot
the man's is he's, HE plus S

explanation.surface: A man taking drugs ends up with a habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' and 'dope' together suggest addiction, but habit here is dress, as in a monk's habit. 'Leading to' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a distinctive garment, so the word stands for garments generally.

clue.text: Body of Church unaltered accommodating Saint

indicators.note: accommodating says the saint letter is housed within the phrase for unaltered

parts.note: as is means unaltered, left in its state

explanation.surface: A church body stays unchanged while making room for a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body of Church' reads as a congregation; 'Body' alone is the definition, a vehicle's frame.
explanation.definitionFit: The chassis is the base frame of a car or other vehicle, its structural body.

clue.text: Overthrow welcoming execution over exile

indicators.note: welcoming says the word for overthrow takes the other in

parts.note: to oust is to overthrow or expel

indicators.note: over says the word for execution is turned back to front

parts.note: an act is a performance, an execution of something

explanation.surface: A coup that brings an execution ends with someone banished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execution' is a performance, an act, not a killing.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is someone rejected by society, a person sent into exile.

clue.text: Initially having abandoned speed, takes excessive speed

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the following five words

parts.note: speed as a noun, rapidity

explanation.surface: Having given up on speed, someone takes it to excess.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'speed' is part of the letter run; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is hurry, excessive rapidity of action, so it means swiftness.

clue.text: Feeling excited about new issue raised

indicators.note: about says the word for excited goes round the other pieces

parts.note: sent is slang for transported, thrilled, excited

indicators.note: raised in a down clue says the pieces are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to emit is to issue or give out

explanation.surface: Emotions run high over a fresh matter that has been brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' as sent is the slang sense of thrilled, carried away; 'raised' turns the new-plus-issue pair upwards to give TIMEN before 'about' wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is an emotion or attitude, a feeling about something.

clue.text: Device dumps after glitch returns

indicators.note: after places the word for dumps behind the other piece
returns says the word for glitch comes back, read right to left

parts.note: a bug is a glitch in software
rubbish dumps are bins

explanation.surface: A gadget is thrown away after a fault keeps coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: Gubbins is British slang for a gadget or contraption whose name you cannot recall.

clue.text: Boss dropping right clanger

indicators.note: dropping says the letter for right falls out of the word for boss

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for boss or foreman

explanation.surface: The boss makes a clanger by dropping the right thing.
explanation.walkthrough: A clanger is a British word for a blunder; a gaffer is a British slang boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is an embarrassing blunder, what Britons call dropping a clanger.

clue.text: Undergarment that is about below neck

indicators.note: below in a down clue puts those pieces underneath the word for neck

parts.note: brass and neck are both British slang for cheek or nerve, as in brass neck
IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An undergarment that sits just under the neckline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below neck' looks like where the garment sits; neck means brass, nerve, as in British 'brass neck'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassiere is a woman's supporting undergarment for the breasts, a bra.

clue.text: Entering artist quarter

parts.note: Ingres was a French Neoclassical painter
S, south, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Moving into the artists' quarter of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist quarter' suggests a bohemian district; read as artist plus quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is the act of going in, an entrance, so it matches entering used as a noun.

clue.text: Endless end assumed, assuming rising misery

indicators.note: rising in a down clue says the letters are read upwards, backwards
assuming means taking on, so the clue words take the answer within them

explanation.surface: An endless end is accepted, bringing ever-growing gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assuming' holds SSENDAS in 'endleSS END ASsumed'; 'rising' turns it back.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadness is sorrow or unhappiness, the condition of being wretched.

clue.text: Mechanic needed with fan losing power

indicators.note: losing says the letter for power drops out of the word for fan

parts.note: a partisan is a devoted supporter, a fan
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A mechanic is wanted, along with a fan that has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'fan' a cooling fan with failed power; it is a supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanic in its older sense is a manual worker or craftsman, a skilled tradesperson.

clue.text: Possibly having standards lowered?

parts.note: flags are standards, so a place decked with them could be so described; the word also means drooped or tired, as if lowered

explanation.surface: A question about someone whose moral standards may have slipped.
explanation.walkthrough: Standards look like moral principles; they are banners. The adjective also means wilting or flagging in energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to droop or weaken, and a flagged path or building could be one hung with banners.

clue.text: Drink nearly undiluted drop in vacant solitude

indicators.note: in places the other pieces inside the emptied word
vacant empties the word solitude, leaving only its outer letters
nearly says the word for undiluted loses its final letter

parts.note: naked means plain, with nothing added, so undiluted
a drop is a small amount, a bit

explanation.surface: A drinker takes a nearly neat drop in lonely isolation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly undiluted' looks like a description of the drink, but it is wordplay: naked in the sense of unmixed, docked by 'nearly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakebite is a British pub drink of lager mixed with cider, sometimes with a dash of blackcurrant.

clue.text: Rocked for the audience in leather

indicators.note: for the audience says the word is heard, not seen, so we need its sound-alike

parts.note: rocked means swayed, moved to and fro

explanation.surface: A rock band played to the crowd dressed in leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocked' suggests a rock concert, but it means swayed, a near sound-alike of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather with a napped finish, made from the underside of the hide.

clue.text: Ancient texts are old custom almost rejected

indicators.note: rejected says the joined pieces are turned back to front

parts.note: art is the archaic form of are, as in thou art

indicators.note: almost says the word for custom loses its last letter

parts.note: use is custom or habit, as in usage

explanation.surface: Ancient writings are an old custom that has almost been cast aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' belongs with 'are', marking the archaic form ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutras are aphorisms or collections of teachings in Hindu and Buddhist scripture, ancient sacred writings.

clue.text: Rare butterfly effect's start around butterfly's opening

indicators.note: around says the first pieces are wrapped about the other letter

parts.note: the red admiral is a butterfly

indicators.note: opening takes the first letter of the word butterfly's
start takes the first letter of the word effect's

explanation.surface: The butterfly effect starts with a rare butterfly's first flap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butterfly effect' reads as chaos theory; 'butterfly' alone is the admiral.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare in the sense of exceptionally fine or excellent, deserving praise.

clue.text: Seconds after otherwise eating balanced snack

indicators.note: after puts the seconds letter behind the rest
eating says the word for otherwise takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: else means otherwise, as in or else
even means balanced, level

explanation.surface: Second helpings follow a balanced diet, otherwise it is just a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack and cup of tea, taken around eleven o'clock.

clue.text: Queen single in start cut being faulty

parts.note: ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: in says the word for single goes inside
cut says the word for start loses its last letter

parts.note: to rouse is to start, as in starting game from cover
one is single

explanation.surface: A queen, alone at the start, having been cut down for being flawed.
explanation.definitionFit: Erroneous means wrong or mistaken, containing errors.

clue.text: Bounds, more cocky, embracing yours truly's sweetheart

indicators.note: embracing says the word for more cocky goes round the other pieces

parts.note: perter is more pert, cheekier or cockier
yours truly is the setter, so yours truly's gives I'm
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Someone cheekier holds the setter's beloved within limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' reads as a lover; split it as sweet's heart, its middle letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: A perimeter is the boundary of an area, its bounds or outer limits.

clue.text: Probes knights perhaps surrounding rook

indicators.note: surrounding says the word for knights goes round the rook letter

parts.note: knights are an example of chess pieces, hence perhaps
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess player probes with knights circling a rook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks knights as an example of pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to penetrate, so pierces and probes both mean pushes into.

clue.text: Weed garden's first bed raised in grass

indicators.note: in places the other pieces inside the word for grass

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing, to rat

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word garden's
raised in a down clue says the word for bed is read upwards

parts.note: a row is a bed in a vegetable garden, a planted strip

explanation.surface: A weed from the garden's first raised bed sits in the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is the informing verb, as in British 'to grass on someone'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragwort is a yellow-flowered plant, poisonous to livestock, widely treated as a weed.

clue.text: Made money without station ultimately having listeners

indicators.note: without says that letter is removed from the word for made money

parts.note: earned means made money from work

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word station

explanation.surface: A radio station made money without ever having an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listeners' suggests a radio audience; here it means ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Listeners is a playful word for ears, so something with ears, like a jug or corn, is so described.

clue.text: More bitter, shown up accepting European withdrawal

indicators.note: accepting says the reversed word takes the European letter in
shown up in a down clue says the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: tarter means sharper, more bitter

explanation.surface: A more bitter figure, exposed, accepts a European pull-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shown up' looks like being exposed; it means turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is an army's withdrawal from a position.

clue.text: Outrage seeing 'fake news' contains nothing

parts.note: a dud is a fake, a counterfeit

indicators.note: contains says the word for news holds the nothing letter

parts.note: gen is British slang for information or news
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Fury at fake news that turns out to contain nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks bind 'fake news' as one phrase, but the two words work separately; gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudgeon is a feeling of deep resentment, as in high dudgeon, so indignation.

clue.text: Composer's eulogy airs occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally takes letters now and then, here every other one starting with the first

explanation.surface: A composer's funeral tribute is broadcast from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Elgar was the English composer of the Enigma Variations and Pomp and Circumstance.

clue.text: Ignorant reportedly get a peerage

indicators.note: reportedly says what we hear, so the phrase is replaced by its sound-alike

parts.note: to be knighted is to receive an honour, loosely a peerage

explanation.surface: An ignorant person is said to be heading for the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jibes at honours for the undeserving; strictly a knighthood is not a peerage, but the sound fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Benighted means in intellectual darkness, unenlightened, lacking knowledge.

clue.text: Powerful heartless tyrant besieging resistance

indicators.note: besieging says the shortened word surrounds the resistance letter
heartless removes the middle letter of the word for tyrant

parts.note: a bully is a petty tyrant
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A mighty, cruel tyrant lays siege to the resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Burly describes someone big and strong, of a sturdy, muscular build.

clue.text: Enjoyment is over following sudden wind

indicators.note: following puts the over letter after the word for wind

parts.note: a gust is a sudden rush of wind
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: The fun is over once a sudden wind blows.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty relish or zest in doing something.

clue.text: Chapter by person launching garments

parts.note: a lobber is one who lobs, launching something high

explanation.surface: A chapter is written by someone launching a clothing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Launching garments' looks like starting a fashion range; a lobber launches a ball. Clobber is British slang for clothes and gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is British informal slang for clothes or belongings, so it covers garments.

clue.text: Indecent old boy sighted, we hear

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: we hear says the word for sighted is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: sighted means seen

explanation.surface: An old boy was spotted, so rumour has it, being indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive to decency, especially sexually, so indecent in a strong sense.

clue.text: Fasten belt finally covered by some fullness

indicators.note: covered by says those pieces sit inside the word for some

parts.note: say means some, roughly, as in say fifty people
to tie is to fasten

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word belt

explanation.surface: Fastening a belt at last hides some fullness after a big meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' as SAY is the sense of approximately, about.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiety is the state of being fed to the full, satisfied beyond hunger.

clue.text: Reduce some anguish or tension

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Cutting down on some of life's anguish or stress.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten something is to make it less long, cutting or reducing it.
